senses: A former unit to measure the intensity of light, approximately 9.74 candelas.
ety: Named after the inventor of the Carcel lamp.
examples: When experimenting in Paris with a No. 3 lamp in a vertical direction, it showed a consumption of 34.6 liters (1.2 cubic feet) per carcel obtained.
In all systems of lighting, save electricity, the unit of light is the carcel.

senses: A Holden Commodore.
ety: From Commodore (“name of a car model”) + -ie (“diminutive suffix”).

senses: Having swirls; swirling.
A female ninja.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese くノ一(いち) (kunoichi).

senses: One who, or that which, upholds or supports; a prop.
One who, or that which, stays, stops, or restrains.
Wearing a cockade.
A Roman unit of mass, usually equivalent to 327 g.
A traditional Spanish unit of mass, usually around 460 g.
A traditional Portuguese unit of mass, usually equivalent to 345 g and particularly used for trade in medicines.
Synonym of arratel, a separate Portuguese unit of mass, usually around 460 g.
Synonym of pound, a notional pound of silver as a money of account, especially in medieval contexts.
ety: From Latin lībra (“pound”), partially via Italian, Spanish, and Portuguese libra. Doublet of arratel, libbra, Libra, lira, litra, litre, livre, and rottol.

senses: A source of nourishment; food.
Something that promotes growth or development; a nutrient.
ety: Inherited from Middle English nutriment, from Latin nūtrīmentum.

senses: The music for either of these dances.
ety: Borrowed from French sarabande, from Spanish zarabanda.

senses: concrete conveyed through a hose and pneumatically projected at high velocity onto a surface.
ety: Blend of shot + concrete. First attested use is in a report at the 1934 convention of the American Railway Engineering Association.
examples: After each blast, rubble is taken out, and the excavated area is covered in a waterproof membrane and sprayed with shotcrete.

senses: In Japanese architecture, a V-shaped finial used mainly on Shinto shrine roofs.
The rank or status of a captain.
The jurisdiction of a captain.
An administrative division of the former Spanish and Portuguese colonial empires.
ety: From captain + -cy. Piecewise doublet of chieftaincy.
examples: He obtains a captaincy in the Catalonian army
The territory bathed by this river belongs to the captaincy of Benito Maciel the father.

senses: One who loads cargo onto a vessel.
Eager to communicate; talkative.
Something mysterious and dangerous.
ety: Nonsense word from The Hunting of the Snark by Lewis Carroll.

senses: A proponent of ethnonationalism.
examples: As central Party control weakened, independence demands grew in other republike, inspired in part by local ethnonationalisms and fear of living in a Yugoslavia dominated by Serbian ethnonationalists.

This election is a hint of one way things could turn next: a new split between the beneficiaries of multicultural globalism and the working-class ethnonationalists who feel left behind economically and culturally.

senses: A motorized rickshaw of South Asia and East Asia, often available for hire in the manner of a taxi.
An unfriendly or suspicious glance.
An undesirable effect in paint, particularly automotive finishes, normally caused by oil or other contaminants on the painted surface.
An undesirable dull appearance in the table of a diamond that has been cut too shallow.
Having quills or similar structures.
Having long, narrow petals or florets.
Created through the process of quilling.
Having small, rounded folds.
Decorated with quillwork.
examples: In Ireland have I seen this stubborn Cade Oppose himself against a troop of kerns, And fought so long till that his thighs with darts Were almost like a sharp-quill'd porpentine;
He leaned down to inspect a white-quilled cactus, and then spotted a different kind with skinnier branches and only a few drab spines.
A quilled lionfish was face to face with a saurian moray eel, sizing it up before swimming on.

senses: Any organism that is parasitic during part of its life cycle, especially one that eventually kills its host.
examples: All of these solitary parasitoid wasps that use their sting-ovipositors for stinging prey and depositing eggs are subjected to little predatory pressure from large predators.

senses: One who performs powerlifting.
An obsolete French unit of power, equal to the power required to raise a quintal at a velocity of one metre per second.
Any shell-shaped structure
An apse, or the plain semidome of an apse.
ety: Borrowed from Late Latin concha (“a mussel shell”). Doublet of conch.

senses: Spanish chain, a traditional Spanish and Mexican unit of distance equivalent to about 41.9 m.
ety: From Spanish cordel (“surveying rope, 50 varas”), from Catalan cordell (“cord, string”), from Vulgar Latin *cordellus (“little rope”), from Latin chorda (“rope, cord”) + -ellus (“-elle: forming diminutives”). Equivalent to cord + -el.

senses: A ball of cooked rice mixed with ghee and black sesame seeds offered to ancestors during Hindu funeral rites and ancestor worship rituals.
The wife of the dauphin; dauphiness.
ety: Borrowed from French dauphine, equivalent to dauphin + -ine.

senses: A code that serves to unlock something, such as an electronic door or a car stereo (as an antitheft measure).
A female water spirit that leads handsome men to their deaths underwater.
ety: From Russian руса́лка (rusálka, “mermaid, siren”). Doublet of rosalia.
examples: She is now a rusalka, a water spirit; in revenge she sends their daughter, a rusalochka, to lure him into the water.

senses: A black or dark green aphid (Aphis fabae) that is a common pest of agricultural crops.
A focus on the development of melody
examples: No sense of aloofness or distance diluted his warm melodicism.

senses: A strong distilled alcoholic beverage made from various fruits, varieties of which (such as slivovitz) are found across the Balkans and the Mediterranean.
ety: Borrowed from Serbo-Croatian rakija/ракија, from Ottoman Turkish راقی (rakı), assumed from Arabic عَرَق (ʕaraq, “sweat; wine”) (as rakija or wine vapor drops are similar to drops of sweat). Doublet of raki.

senses: A convex line or surface.
One who or that which iterates.
Having no friends; friendless.
examples: Not another word could he be induced to utter, and he seemed as unfriended and one might say unfriendable as a frost-bitten Arctic explorer astray on an ice-floe.

senses: Sorghum syrup.
ety: From New Latin genus name Sorghum, from Italian sorgo, from Vulgar Latin *syricum (“Syrian”), from Sȳricus. Doublet of the synonyms sorgho (via French) and sorgo (via Italian).

senses: One who shirks a duty or responsibility.

A code; a charter; a grant of privileges.
A custom having the force of law.
A declaration by a magistrate.
A place where justice is administered.
The jurisdiction of a tribunal

senses: Arabian jasmine (Jasminum sambac).
ety: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish sampaguita, from sampaga + -ita.
